answer: Under reticulated-duel enrollment, each new identity must win a timed puzzle duel against every other identity enrolled in the same rolling hour, so mass joiners force each fake identity into exponentially many pairwise duels (duel count grows with cohort size squared). Ten coordinated fakes trigger forty-five duels at a jetty checkpoint, while one hundred trigger nearly five thousand across the bridge cohort, so bots cannot wander in cheaply. A lone honest joiner faces only that hour's small pool, pays one fair share, and proves liveness once.
